added.title: Environmental Health Safety Specialist
added.description:
EHS Professional – Construction Safety Specialist
Teklus Construction | Reno, NV | Full-Time | On-Site | $75,000–$85,000/year | Positions Open: 1

Teklus is a veteran-owned and veteran-operated general contractor out of Reno - about 40 people building commercial and industrial projects across Nevada, Arizona, Kansas, and California, including work for some of the biggest names in the tech industry. People join for the client list. They stay because of how they're treated.

We're hiring an EHS Professional to own on-shift safety oversight for a major Reno-based operation with a direct focus on fall protection, equipment safety, and OSHA compliance.

How we work - the five things we hire for

Treat Everyone Kind Like U Should.
No matter who they are - lead with kindness, listen genuinely, give credit in abundance, and be straight with people - especially when it's hard.
Have Trust, Give Trust.
Trust goes both ways - believe in others' good intentions and follow through so clients and teammates can count on what we say.
Build It Like It's Yours.
Never settle for good enough - build every job like our name is on it and have the courage to always do what's right.
Take the Extra Minute.
Rushing costs more than it saves - pause to check your work, keep everyone safe from harm, and celebrate our successes.
A Little Better All the Time.
We're never done learning - the smallest lessons, applied every day, are why each project runs better than the last.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Provide on-shift oversight of fall protection compliance, equipment use, and safe work sequencing
Develop, review, and approve Job Hazard Analyses (JHAs) and Pre-Task Safety Plans
Conduct daily inspections of fall protection systems, anchor points, and PPE
Audit confined space entries, hot work, and elevated work permits
Investigate near-misses and incidents; document findings and drive corrective actions
Monitor weather and ambient conditions; issue timely safety alerts to field and client teams
Lead toolbox talks, safety briefings, and new-hire safety orientations
Maintain training records, SDS library, and OSHA 300 logs
Manage permit-to-work systems: hot work, confined space, LOTO, elevated work, excavation
Conduct industrial hygiene monitoring (noise, dust, heat stress)

WHAT YOU BRING

Required:
Bachelor's degree in Occupational Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Environmental Science, Engineering, or related field ( or equivalent experience
)
3+ years of EHS experience in construction or heavy industrial settings
OSHA 30-Hour Construction certification
Current First Aid, CPR, and AED certification
Working knowledge of OSHA 1910/1926, EPA, and DOT requirements

Preferred:
CHST, STSC, ASP, GSP, or CSP certification
Authorized OSHA Outreach Trainer (10/30-Hour Construction)
Experience with permit-to-work systems or behavior-based safety programs
Background in fall protection or access-point safety work

BENEFITS

401(k), Roth IRA, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, parental leave, OT pay, sick time, and paid time off.

ABOUT TEKLUS CONSTRUCTION

Teklus Construction is a Reno-based general contractor licensed in Arizona, Nevada, Kansas, and California, and a proud Veteran-Owned & Veteran-Operated company specializing in commercial and industrial construction general contracting, project planning, quality control, and
project close-out.

The statements contained in this job description are not intended to be a comprehensive list of every duty, responsibility, or qualification associated with the position. Duties may be added, modified, or removed at the discretion of management based on operational needs.

Teklus Construction is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

added.title: 72D Environmental Scientist
added.description:
Job Description

The environment we live in has a huge impact on our health. Think about it. Is the air we breathe clean? Is the water contaminated? How will temperature and moisture levels affect the growth of toxic molds? It is for these reasons, along with myriad others, that the Army National Guard needs Environmental Scientists to join our team of Medical Corps Officers. As an Environmental Scientist and an Officer on the U.S. Army Health Care Team, your knowledge of biology, environmental health, and industrial hygiene will help prevent illness and injury. Now is your chance to ensure the health and vitality of the men and women who stand ready to respond when something threatens the community, the State, or the Nation. But you won't stand apart from these heroes. You will stand among them as a commissioned Medical Corps Officer in the Army National Guard. In so doing, you will increase your knowledge and learn the latest techniques in our collaborative environment. When you practice in your community and serve when needed, you'll enhance your skills by working alongside health care professionals who share your passion for excellence while eliminating the distractions typically found in a civilian practice, such as office management or overhead. Earn While You Learn
The Army National Guard Medical Team can be a great place to start your health care career or an inspiring place to lead others with your experience and expertise. Either way, it's an outstanding way to serve your country and help others. Medical Professional Officers are required to complete an initial military orientation and training course lasting 26 days in San Antonio, TX, at Fort Sam Houston. The trainers are fellow Medical Professional Officers.

Benefits/Requirements

Benefits

Medical and dental care for you and your family (TRICARE Reserve Select)
Up to $400,000 in low-cost life insurance
Discounted and tax-free grocery and shopping privileges at post exchanges and commissaries
Free military air flights based on space availability
Free academic testing and counseling for spouse
Access to recreational facilities on military installations
A retirement pension plan at the completion of 20 years of part-time service

Requirements

Meet the prescribed medical and moral standards for appointment as a commissioned Officer
Be a United States citizen
Have completed an accredited qualifying degree program
Be 21 years of age
Some Advanced Practice Medical Professionals may join up to age 58
Be able to obtain a secret security clearance

Applicants must meet minimum qualifications. Actual assignment may depend on position availability.

Most non-prior service candidates will earn between $196.26 and $254.91 per drill weekend

Programs and benefits are subject to change.

added.title: Environmental Specialist
added.description:
We are seeking an Environmental Specialist
for one of our clients operating a large-scale industrial facility in California. This is a hands-on role supporting a complex environmental program, with a particular focus on water compliance, monitoring, and groundwater-related activities. You will work closely with EHS, operations, engineering, and external partners to manage environmental requirements and strengthen compliance as the organization continues to grow.

Key Responsibilities:

Support water and groundwater monitoring, sampling, testing, and compliance activities across facility operations.
Coordinate environmental sampling activities and work with laboratories, consultants, and contractors to ensure accurate and timely results.
Collect, analyze, and maintain water quality and environmental data to support regulatory reporting and compliance requirements.
Support groundwater monitoring and remediation-related programs, including coordination with environmental consultants and technical teams.
Prepare technical reports, regulatory documentation, and records associated with water and environmental compliance programs.
Conduct facility inspections and identify potential environmental compliance issues and corrective actions.
Support environmental permitting, regulatory reporting, audits, and agency inspections.
Maintain organized environmental records and documentation to support regulatory and internal requirements.
Support environmental incident investigations and continuous improvement initiatives.
Collaborate with operations, engineering, and EHS teams to integrate environmental requirements into day-to-day facility activities.

The ideal candidate will have 3+ years of experience in water, environmental compliance, or a related environmental role within an industrial setting, with hands-on experience supporting water quality monitoring, sampling, regulatory reporting, and compliance programs. Experience within mining, chemical processing, or other heavy industrial operations is preferred. Experience working within California’s environmental regulatory environment and with state or regional water agencies is a strong plus.

This is an opportunity to take on a meaningful role within a growing industrial operation and gain exposure to a complex, high-impact water and environmental program. In return, the company offers a competitive compensation package including base salary, annual bonus, and equity.
